texts.preamble: The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Gajanand Kushwah on 3 December, 2025 Author: Milind Ramesh Phadke Bench: Milind Ramesh Phadke Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:31720 1 Mc In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke On The 3 rd Of December, 2025 Misc. Criminal Case No. 3051 of 2015 The State Of Madhya Pradesh Versus Gajanand Kushwah Appearance: Shri Samar Ghuraiya - Public Prosecutor for State. Shri Sourabh Agarwal - Advocate for respondent. Order The present application under Section 378(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code for leave to appeal has been filed by the State against the order dated 30.12.2014 passed in Case No. 2294/2011, whereby the respondent was acquitted of the charges under Sections 7(1) read with 16(1) (A)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
texts.facts: Order The present application under Section 378(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code for leave to appeal has been filed by the State against the order dated 30.12.2014 passed in Case No. 2294/2011, whereby the respondent was acquitted of the charges under Sections 7(1) read with 16(1) (A)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The prosecution's case, in brief, is that on 07.05.2011, at approximately 2:15 PM, Food Inspector Naveen Jain conducted an inspection of the accused's ice-cream factory and requested the license for selling food from the accused, who produced receipt No. 007, Book No. 11, dated 14.04.2011, issued by the Municipal Council. With the vendor's consent, the inspection was carried out in the presence of witnesses. During the inspection, the vendor was found to be manufacturing, storing, and selling various types of ice-cream for human consumption. With the vendor's consent, a sample of the ice-cream was taken for standard quality NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31720 2 MCRC-3051-2015 testing, with the total cost of Rs. 72/- paid in cash to the vendor and a receipt obtained. The ice-cream mixture was thoroughly homogenized, divided into three equal parts, and properly packed, with a panchnama drawn up. According to the examination report of the ice-cream sample submitted by the Deputy Director, Food and Drug Administration, District Guna, under letter dated 13.07.2011, the sample was found to be adulterated. Following this, after obtaining proper sanction for prosecution, a complaint was filed against the accused in the court of law. The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Gajanand Kushwah on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165579606/ 1 However, the learned subordinate court, after a careful evaluation of the evidence, rendered a judgment of acquittal. Learned counsel for the State submitted that the accused had already received the notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. It was contended that although the original receipt of the postal dispatch sent to the accused from the post office was not exhibited in the case record, the accused did not raise any objection during the proceedings claiming that they were denied an opportunity to have the sample tested at another branch of the Central Laboratory. It was further submitted that the Food Inspector, Naveen Jain, had fully corroborated the prosecution case and occurrence, and that witness Jitendra Saxena had also verified the compliance with the requirements of Section 13(2).
texts.arguments: Learned counsel emphasized that there was no material contradiction in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, which could negate the charges established against the accused. Learned counsel for the respondent contended that the trial court, after a careful and thorough examination of the evidence on record, rightly acquitted the respondent of the alleged offences. During arguments, the accused cited the judgment of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31720 4 MCRC-3051-2015 Coordinate Bench in Ramesh Agrawal v. State of M.P., 2014 F.A.J. 47, wherein it was held that merely dispatching the report to the accused is not sufficient.
